program.topic: caller-bound effect authority across execution-generation turnover

fresh_internal_evidence.claim: V14 admits stale first-start, stale retry and unbound effect attempts into COMMITTING; selected successor requires caller-bound immutable execution-generation authority at reservation, begin/retry and provider-precommit.

mechanism: B2 live presented capability equals reservation binding equals current generation
provider commit window serializes execution release across final B3 check plus provider callback
post-turnover outcome reconciliation remains observation authority, not retry authority
ClayCode caller-bound semantic contract is present but compiler/lowering promotion remains unproven

external_primary_evidence.source: Mike Burrows, The Chubby lock service for loosely-coupled distributed systems, OSDI 2006
external_primary_evidence.relevance: Downstream protected operations use an opaque sequencer carrying lock generation rather than mere observation of current lock state; supports explicit fencing at the effect boundary.
POST timeout can leave outcome uncertain; idempotency identifies repeated requests but does not itself establish current execution ownership.

external_primary_evidence.source: AWS Builders Library, Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
external_primary_evidence.relevance: Timeout after a possibly accepted effect requires idempotent retry semantics or reconciliation; supports separating outcome recovery from execution authority.

flock locks are attached to open file descriptions and are inherited through fork. No current repository fork/multiprocessing/process-pool runtime path was found, so process-incarnation hardening is retained as a conditional future release obligation rather than added now.

hypothesis.statement: A sufficient Frank effect fence requires possession of a live Gate-issued execution capability, immutable reservation binding to that capability generation, and a final provider-precommit recheck; equality of caller-supplied epoch/session/client values is insufficient.
hypothesis.prediction: A caller with copied generation scalars but no live lease/flock can pass the legacy V16.1 raw-field fence, while a Gate-issued exact-object successor rejects copied/constructed lease objects.

strongest_counterhypothesis.statement: Matching current lease_epoch plus holder session/client is sufficient internal execution authority because only trusted Frank runtime code can call the lifecycle API.
strongest_counterhypothesis.falsifier: Present a copied tuple from a legitimate current holder through a structurally separate caller that does not possess the live lease object or physical flock handle.

new_adversarial_finding.observation: At head e04b88cfcd0f3dc24f9afc829046464b281a0811 and still at d7759b63c8a8ecf4995f577fc9cbf459c40cc8ab, FrankExecutionLease.__init__ is public and derive_execution_generation_fence accepts any live-looking FrankExecutionLease instance. counterevidence_and_limits: The exact-object WeakSet registry is a trusted-runtime discipline, not a hostile Python introspection security boundary.

Linux flock and the registry can both be inherited across fork. No current repository runtime path using multiprocessing, os.fork, ProcessPoolExecutor or uvicorn workers was found. If a forking execution path is introduced, add process-incarnation or at-fork invalidation and a corresponding regression before release.

PR204 has added a provider commit critical section after the initial B3 design, closing a distinct check-then-release TOCTOU class. This is complementary to Gate-issued object identity and must be preserved.

ClayCode static contract text is not compiler/lowering evidence. F-V01-09 cannot close until the strict caller-bound path is the ordinary compiled/lowered effect route and the legacy unbound V14 production attempt path is unreachable.

final_synthesis: The executed target-compatible evidence changes the architecture decision: an execution generation is not sufficient when represented only as caller-copyable scalars. The effect boundary needs a non-transferable live execution capability, immutable birth-generation binding, final provider-boundary revalidation, and reconciliation-only recovery after uncertain provider contact. PR204 supplies most of that causal chain and has independently added release serialization across provider commit. Its remaining B0 object-issuance gap is isolated by PR217. No promotion is justified until PR217 executes green on the target lane and the same contract is proven through actual ClayCode lowering with legacy unbound product paths unreachable.
